title: Pull a board to retrieve an out-of-reach jar
instruction: Put the spice jar in the basket.
context: An item can be out of reach even when the surface supporting it is reachable. Pulling the board brings the jar close enough to pick up, as when retrieving something from the far end of a tray or placemat.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y to the left; arm bases at x 0, y +-0.305 m). Board: a cut length of pine 1x3 lumber (actual 19 x 64 mm), 48 cm long, painted green, 0.27 kg, loose, lying flat along x on the midline (y 0) with its near end 0.34 m and its far end 0.82 m in front of the arm bases. Spice jar: small squat glass jar with lid, 4.5 cm diameter, 6 cm tall, 0.10 kg, red, loose, standing upright on the board with its centre 0.78 m in front of the arm bases on the midline (4 cm from the board's far end). Basket: open plastic basket, blue, outer 15.2 x 15.2 cm, inner 14 x 14 cm, 0.4 cm floor, 0.6 cm thick walls rising 5.6 cm above the floor (rim 6.0 cm above the table), fixed (taped down), centred at x 0.30 m, y 0.25 m (in front of the left arm). Nothing else on the table. The jar starts beyond either arm's reach in any gripper orientation; the board's near end is within reach of both arms.
scoring: 1.0 if the jar rests in the basket: its centre over the basket's inner 14 x 14 cm, its bottom within 1 cm of the basket floor, still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s, and let go (both grippers at least 3 cm from the jar); the trial then ends. Otherwise, at the end of the run: 0.4 if the jar is on the board or the table, or held above it, with its centre at most 0.40 m in front of the arm bases and at most 0.40 m to either side of the midline (within both arms' reach); 0 if the jar is anywhere else, including still out on the far part of the board or table; 0 if the jar has fallen off the table (its bottom more than 2 cm below the table top or its centre outside the table).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the board back with its near end 0.34 m out on the midline and the jar upright 0.78 m out on it; mark both positions on the table with tape.
fidelity: Rigid primitives: the board is one box, the jar one cylinder, the basket five fixed boxes (real baskets have tapered or perforated walls). Every loose object uses the simulator's single default rubber-like material (static friction 1.2, dynamic 1.0); real pine on a laminate table slides more easily, and a glass jar on pine grips less, so in the real world pull slowly. The basket is fixed in place, as if taped down. The board's paint and the jar's lid and label are a single flat colour each.
